title: App sign-in with unsaved changes
summary: Diceroll's App sign-in with two edits waiting for Save: Apple turned off by the operator (the row says 'Off by you' with 'Use the default', and a caution about App Store guideline 4.8) and Email moved from Optional to Required, which takes the value over from the manifest. The SaveBar names both changes and says players are asked again.
compare: Save model: Sign-in methods, What Diceroll gets, License keys and Customer portal are one resource (the product's sign-in settings), so their controls only mark the page dirty and one SaveBar lists every change by section. The Status switch is the Sign-in feature and applies on its own (turning it off asks first: identity.sign-in-off). The product connection is edited in its own dialog from 'Edit'. 'Inside the game' rows have no control.

A changed row carries an accent bar at its leading edge and 'Not saved' under its text; the rail puts a dot after each section with changes. Leaving the page with changes asks first (useUnsavedChangesGuard).

An overridden derived provider reads 'Off by you. Diceroll ships on the App Store, so Apple would be on.' with 'Use the default'; after Save the row keeps 'Off by you' and the link, and the derived reason returns only when the default is used again.

Turning Apple off for a product that ships on iOS while Google or Steam stays on shows the caution under the row at once, before Save, citing App Store Review Guideline 4.8. It is a caution, not a block: Save stays available.

A value set by identity.claims in .pkey/product says it was taken from the manifest ('was Optional in .pkey/product'); after Save its section shows 'Changed here' and 'Revert to manifest…', as License keys does on identity.app-sign-in.

The SaveBar sticks to the bottom of the window inside the cards column: the count, each change in words with its section, the consequence for players ('asked what to share again at their next sign-in'; the share who must now share their email), 'Discard' and 'Save 2 changes'. Saving shows 'Saving…' and then the toast 'Saved 2 changes to App sign-in'.
Phone: the caution spans the card under the row, and the SaveBar's buttons share its last row.
